subject: Region-lock confirmation & subprocessor audit timeline
messages:
From: Emily Jacobs <emily.j@konnecthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@konnect.health
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: EU-only serving + subprocessor vetting process

Hi Ben —

We're finalizing our vendor matrix for the pilot. A few quick asks from our security team before we proceed to PO:

- Can Redwood provide a firm commitment that Konnect Health's production request/responses are pinned to EU-only hosts (no transient cross-border processing) except for the limited backup window described below?
- If there is a transient failover (e.g., 72h failover), can you confirm the notification cadence and the operator/role that will be alerted?
- Please share a recent subprocessor roster and a short description of your vendor vetting steps for subprocessors that handle telemetry/analytics.

We have a procurement deadline Friday; if we can get a timeline and a DPA addendum draft today or tomorrow, that would help.

Thanks —
Emily
Emily Jacobs
Director of SRE, Konnect Health
emily.j@konnecthealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Request: EU-only serving + subprocessor vetting process

Folks — forwarding Konnect's ask (below). Procurement wants an answer fast (they're targeting Friday). High level: they need an EU-residency pin for production, a clear operator notification plan for transient failovers, and a recent subprocessor roster + vetting bullets.

Can Legal draft a short DPA addendum that:
- Commits to EU-region serving for production traffic (describe allowed transient failovers and required notifications)
- Captures subprocessor disclosure cadence and right-to-audit language

Rishi/Marissa — can you pull the latest subprocessor roster and a one-paragraph bullet on how we vet analytics/telemetry vendors? If we can attach the roster + draft addendum to a reply to Emily, that should keep procurement moving.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only serving + subprocessor vetting process

Ben —

Thanks for the ping. I drafted a short DPA addendum that:

1) Commits to EU-region serving for production workloads tied to Konnect's account id, with the following carveouts:
   - Operational telemetry (high-level metrics) remains aggregated and anonymized and is only processed in EU.
   - Temporary failover: Redwood may route requests to a non-EU region for up to 72 hours in the case of catastrophic regional outage. We will: notify Konnect's security contact and procurement within 2 hours of failover; provide hourly status updates; and replicate logs back to EU locations once restoration begins.

2) Operator notification: primary escalation goes to the on-call Site Reliability Lead (designated operator role). We will provide a named operator contact prior to production cutover and include a secondary ops inbox.

3) Subprocessor disclosures: attach the current roster (Q2 2028) and commit to a 30-day notification before onboarding any new subprocessor that will process Konnect production request/response data. Provide a short vendor-vetting paragraph.

I've attached a redline (DPA_addendum_v1.pdf) and our subprocessor CSV for review. If this matches product/ops intent, Marissa can send to the customer with the roster. If Konnect needs stronger territorial guarantees, we'll require an enterprise addendum (operator isolation + prospective escrow language) and additional SLA terms.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: DPA_addendum_v1.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Jacobs <emily.j@konnecthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, procurement@konnect.health
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Region-lock confirmation & subprocessor audit timeline

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching our DPA addendum draft and the current subprocessor roster (Q2 2028). Quick notes inline:

- EU-only serving: We can commit to pinning Konnect's production traffic to EU hosts (eu-central-1/eu-west-1 clusters) as of cutover.
- Transient failover: the addendum specifies 72h max for a catastrophic failover and a 2-hour notification SLA to your security contact. We will include the named operator (SRE Lead) contact before cutover.
- Subprocessor vetting: Rishi added the vendor vetting blurb — we perform security questionnaire + SOC/SIG reviews for tier-1 vendors and contract language (DPA clauses) for telemetry/analytics providers. We notify customers 30 days before onboarding subprocessors that could touch production payloads.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached DPA_addendum_v1.pdf and the roster.
2) If acceptable, we'll create a DocuSign envelope for Konnect's signature and schedule a quick 20-min call to name the operator contact.

Files attached: DPA_addendum_v1.pdf (redline), subprocessor_roster_q2_2028.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachments: DPA_addendum_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_q2_2028.csv)
From: Emily Jacobs <emily.j@konnecthealth.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@konnect.health
Date: Thu, 8 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region-lock confirmation & subprocessor audit timeline

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the docs. A few clarifications from our security lead:

- 72h failover is acceptable provided the notification cadence is followed and log replication back to EU is verifiable. We'll want a short runbook excerpt (2–3 bullets) describing how you prove logs were re-ingested into EU after failover.
- The 30-day subprocessor notification is fine; can you confirm whether any telemetry vendor has access to raw prompts/outputs? If so, we need confirmation they only receive pseudonymized telemetry hashes.

We are comfortable moving to DocuSign once we get: (a) the 2–3 bullet runbook excerpt for log replication proof, and (b) the telemetry access confirmation.

I'll loop procurement on DocuSign once we have those items.

—Emily
Emily Jacobs
Director of SRE, Konnect Health
